items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: They hired me, what you call, Emmanuel Perez, them. They had some misunderstanding with Billy Moran, the bass player. Yes. And they led Billy Moran. It was Imperial Band.

ctx.x: Before you played with Billy Phillips Dancehall. Yeah, that was one. Yeah. And you were playing guitar in those days. Guitar, yeah. Then you changed the tenor band.

Tenor band, yeah. When did you take up the bass? I had taken up the bass after I put the tenor band on. I had taken up the bass. They hired me, what you call, Emmanuel Perez, them. They had some misunderstanding with Billy Moran, the bass player. Yes. And they led Billy Moran. It was Imperial Band. Huh? It was Imperial. Imperial Band. They hired me and I stayed with them.
Did you have any lessons on the string bass or did you pick that up?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1962-01-31
items.q: they fired Billy Moran for me. Took me in the band, they had a falling out.

ctx.x: The End The End Okay, I'm going to get the date. 31st of January 1962, Eddie Dawson, Type 1. Can you tell us your birth date, Eddie? When were you born? 19...let me see...24th of July. 24th of July. What year would that be? That was...1884. Uh huh. And did any of your family play instruments before you? No, no. Did you pick it up? Just picked it up myself. How old were you when you first started playing? About 18. You bought yourself a bass, did you, or did you make one up, Paul? Uh huh. You bought a bass from a…

So I'll tell you why, they fired Billy Moran for me. Took me in the band, they had a falling out. Which band was that? That was that band they had to call it the... I don't see that band. Whose band was it? Who was the leader? Yeah. Wait now. Billy Moran and let me see who's the leader now. How you call him? He's a trumpet player. Good trumpet player too. Perez was it? Manny Perez. Manny Perez. Manny Perez. Who else was in that band? Do you remember that Eddie? Oh man, that's been Manny Perez, Billy Moran and…

Yes. just like them guys down there on the 135th in the house. I mean, in Harlem, down there, on the 135th, 34th, 32nd, all out there on the sidewalk in the pool hall with them old box bags. You're out of style, you're out of date, boy. I said, what are you talking about, man? I said, he's made in great big letters. E-B-G, my initial, you're dope. He said, listen, the goods are fine. I'm not criticizing the goods, but the style, you're out of style they would wear. That's when pinch bags first come out. Little…

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: I was playing and Manuel Perez was getting all that work out there at Millenboy

ctx.x: You were speaking about Freddie Kepard earlier. What kind of a style? Was he any different to the other trumpet players? No, no.

He played that Dixieland and jazz trumpet just like the rest of them. Yeah. They all have to play that same way, you see, when you play the trumpet. Because when you get in a band, if you're playing trumpet in a band like they was playing then, you'd have to play that style, you know? The only difference was some fellas could play in brass band music and they couldn't play dance music, you see. That's the two different types of music, you see. When there's a straight and a jazz the other way to dance and music,…

Well, I read Piku told us something about playing out there too with Manuel Perez. Oh, yeah, yeah. I played with Piku out there too. Piku said he remembers the same time when Freddie picked up the cornet sometime.
